source: GeoNames CC BY 4.0 modern place IDs, coordinates, featureCode and names; official city/national government histories, municipal sources, the Library of Congress, scholarly historical research, and current 2026 Equatorial Guinea decree, linked per record/period.
selection: 26 distinct contemporary West/Central African capital, historical capital, and government-seat urban settlements: old/new Equatorial Guinea capital is a deliberate two-city exception. All records distinct from staged batches 01–17.
coordinateConvention: GeoNames 2026 modern representative WGS84 lat/lon points, not historical borders, former town sites, municipal jurisdiction centroids or claims of historical political sovereignty.
countryCodeSemantics: present-day GeoNames metadata only; PPLC/PPLG/PPLA must not imply legal/historical capital status at another date.
historicNameScope: Map label names verified only at cited transitions. A-class 1801 labels are modern-name editorial baselines without historical period attestation and must not be interpreted as full no-rename verification.
reviewMethod: Validate official GeoNames IDs/coordinates; check 138 previous IDs; separate former/current capital roles; distinguish new-town establishment, precursor village, official renaming and editor-selected language transitions.
qualityNotes: All 26 IDs are independent P class settlement records and absent from 138 records across batches 01–17; previous files unchanged.

Equatorial Guinea Decree Law No.1/2026 dated 2026-01-02 (government official source) established Ciudad de la Paz as new capital; Malabo remains an independent extant city. GeoNames now encodes Ciudad de la Paz PPLC 12226438 vs Malabo PPLA 2309527.
The former village Oyala GeoNames 2306898 is not a synonym ID/coordinate for the new planned capital ID 12226438.
Benin Porto-Novo PPLC 2392087 (legal capital) and Cotonou PPLG 2394819 (government seat) remain separate; Côte d'Ivoire Yamoussoukro PPLC 2279755 vs Abidjan PPLA 2293538 likewise.

The city now called Suleja was an older namesake Abuja; it is not the modern planned federal capital Abuja ID 2352778. FCDA sources construction around 1980 distinct from Federal Capital Territory legislation 1976.
Monrovia's initial Christopolis rename in 1824 based on US Library of Congress; date at year precision. Do not merge older local Cape Mesurado villages with the 1822 city.
Banjul former Bathurst colonial town from 1816, official rename in 1973; sources disagree February announcement versus April administrative dates, so year-only.
N'Djamena was Fort-Lamy, renamed in 1973; exact November decision/implementation days remain contested so year-only.

Kinshasa former Léopoldville, renamed during 1966; a cabinet announcement planned 30 June, while a secondary citation of 1966-10-03 legal instrument claims 1 July retroactive effective date. Hold exact day.

Yamoussoukro name reportedly established 1919 per national presidency, but alternative municipal/district histories diverge. 1919 selected provisionally and old N'Gokro village linked rather than assigning modern city point and rank to the former settlement.
Nouakchott urban foundation cornerstone 1958-03-05 from published urban planning research; 1957 planning decision and previous coastal village are distinct.
Malabo Spanish-era Santa Isabel naming year is contested between colonial accounts; 1855 is a provisional year, NOT independently confirmed statutory efficacy. Santa Isabel -> Malabo in 1973.

Ciudad de la Paz formerly Oyala as documented in official 2015 appointment decree; 2017 provincial naming law introduced Ciudad de la Paz but exact effectiveness remains year-granular. National capital status starts 2026-01-02, not 2017.
Existing nativeNames multiform only used if independent contemporaneous official city names are attested. Equal English/native string stored once by default.
No new population rankings, city five-grade tiers, historic national affiliations, shifting coordinates, runtime manifests, place tiles, app changes or main updates.

displayTimeline.researchNote: 적도기니 대통령실 2015년 5월 8일 공문은 신규 시 Oyala의 시장과 정부 대표 임명을 기록한다. 옛 Oyala 토착 소취락(GeoNames 2306898)과 현대 계획도시(12226438)는 구분한다.
2017년 Djibloho주 창설 법률안에서 주도 명칭 Ciudad de la Paz를 사용한다고 명시한다. 법안 제출일은 2월 24일이나 명칭의 시행일을 증명하지 않아 2017년 연도로만 선택.

nameSelectionNotes: 도시별 선택된 연혁상 한국어·영어·원어만 names[]에 수록; 검색 별칭과 비선택 어형 제외.
현 GeoNames 국가코드·원천 인구·도시점으로 옛 국경·역사 인구·5등급 도시 중요도를 추정하지 않는다.
기록된 지명 연혁 및 정치수도·정부 소재지·도시 형성·역사 지리의 판정은 서로 별개이다.
현재 국가 수도는 2026-01-02 법령 이후 Ciudad de la Paz. 과거 수도 Malabo의 지명 객체를 삭제·합병하지 않는다.

temporalEligibility.researchNote: 2015년 정부 문건이 Oyala 계획도시의 시장 임명을 확인. 2008년 계획 구상·이웃 토착 마을과 구별하며 시가지는 2015년 이전부터 공사 중일 수 있음.
temporalEligibility.lifecycleCaveat: Settlement urbanization threshold not identical to physical existence or historic rank; staged only.

events.researchDetail: 2026-01-02 법령으로 Ciudad de la Paz가 적도기니 수도가 됐다. 수도 지위의 발생은 2017년의 신도시명 채택과 별개이다.

linkedPlaces.researchNote: GeoNames 2306898의 마을 Oyala 좌표(1.621619,10.833914)와 계획도시 Ciudad de la Paz ID 12226438(1.59250,10.82361)을 합치지 않는다.

displayTimeline.researchNote: 선택한 현대 GeoNames 한국어/영어/원어 형태를 역사적 조사 시작용 편집 기준으로 놓는다. 이 형태가 정확히 해당 과거 연도에 공용 법정명이었는지는 아직 입증되지 않았다. 무개칭·지배권·국가 소속·도시 등급을 뜻하지 않는다.
